newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian police uncover West Bank bomb lab.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian police uncover West Bank bomb lab.

text.p: Palestinian police said on Monday they had uncovered ready-to-use explosives and disguises at a West Bank apartment they suspect was a bomb lab of the anti-Israeli Hamas movement.
They found 30 kilograms of explosives in a device ready to be detonated along with Jewish religious prayer shawls and skullcaps, wigs and Israeli army uniforms.
PLO officials and Israeli security sources say suicide bombers and kidnappers often pose as religious Jews or Israeli soldiers to enter Israel and carry out attacks.
Hamas, the Islamic Resistance Movement opposed to Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat's peace deals with the Jewish state, has carried out suicide bombings that have killed scores of Israelis.
"The stuff that is ready to be used is 30 kg (66 lb) but we found many other raw materials and equipment," said Bethlehem area police chief Colonel Kamal al-Sheikh.
He linked the discovery of the lab to Hamas activist Issa Khalil Shouka, 41, who was killed last week while making a bomb that blew up in his hands.
He said arrests of Shouka's relatives and friends, as well as further investigations, had led to the discovery.
"We found in an apartment building in Beit Sahour a store of explosives and raw materials and equipment to make explosives...We believe they belong to Hamas," the chief said.

"We found live TNT, hydrogen, chemicals, acids, timers and watches as well," Sheikh said. "Only experts can prepare these explosives. They are similar to the explosives we found after Shouka blew himself up."

Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has demanded Arafat do more to crack down on Moslem guerrilla groups opposed to the peace accords. On Sunday, he lashed out at Arafat's Palestinian Authority over the alleged involvement of PLO police in plans to attack Jewish settlers.
The PLO police denied it was involved in attacks against Israelis.
Cooperation between Israeli and Palestinian security forces, stipulated in peace deals since 1993, has broken down since March over the construction of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
"We are continuing our investigation because it is extremely shocking and dangerous to have an explosives factory in an apartment building. This endangers the security of our citizens," Sheikh said.
